title: Standard charts and the twisting module on Proj of a polynomial ring over A
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $m\ge0$, $S=A[x_0,\dots,x_m]$ graded by total degree, and $P=\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ [def-pc-proj]. Put $U_k=D_+(x_k)$ and let $\mathcal O_P(1)$ be the twisting module of [def-pc-projective-space-twist], with its local basis $e_k=e_k^{(1)}$ on $U_k$. Then the $U_k$ cover $P$, each $U_k$ is canonically $\operatorname{Spec}(S_{(x_k)})$ with $S_{(x_k)}$ the degree-zero part of $S_{x_k}$ [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero], and the map $A[Y_l:l\ne k]\to S_{(x_k)}$ sending $Y_l$ to $x_l/x_k$ is an $A$-algebra isomorphism. On $U_k\cap U_l$, $e_l=(x_l/x_k)e_k$; moreover $U_k\cap U_l$ is the basic open of the function $x_l/x_k$ in $U_k$. There is a unique morphism of schemes $q:P\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] (the structure morphism) whose restriction to each $U_k=\operatorname{Spec}(S_{(x_k)})$ is the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(S_{(x_k)})\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ induced by the ring map $A\to S_{(x_k)}$, $a\mapsto a/1$.

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01NG (lemma-standard-covering-projective-space) and Lemma 01M4 (lemma-standard-open) for the charts and their intersections, Lemma 01MB (lemma-proj-scheme) for $D_+(f)\cong\operatorname{Spec}S_{(f)}$, Lemma 01ME (lemma-structure-morphism-proj) for $q$, Lemma 01MS (lemma-when-invertible) for the twisting module on a chart

proof.text: *Notation and the two Proj nodes.* Put $S=A[x_0,\dots,x_m]$ with $\deg x_k=1$, so $S_0=A$ and $S_+=\bigoplus_{n>0}S_n$. The scheme $P=\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ of [def-pc-proj] and the scheme $\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ of [def-nagata-affine-proj] are the same construction (both are Mathlib's \texttt{AlgebraicGeometry.Proj}, with $D_+(f)$ identified with $\operatorname{Spec}S_{(f)}$ by \texttt{Proj.basicOpenIsoSpec}), so the lemmas stated for the latter apply to $P$. Every homogeneous element of positive degree of $S$ is an $A$-linear combination of monomials of positive degree, each divisible by some $x_k$; hence the ideal $S_+$ is generated by the homogeneous elements $x_0,\dots,x_m$ of degree $1$.

*The charts cover $P$ and are affine.* By [prop-nagata-proj-standard-open] applied to $R=S$ and the family $(x_0,\dots,x_m)$, which generates $S_+$ by step 1, the standard opens $U_k=D_+(x_k)$ cover $P$, and each $U_k$ is an open subscheme with a canonical isomorphism $U_k\cong\operatorname{Spec}(S_{(x_k)})$, where $S_{(x_k)}$ is the degree-zero part of $S_{x_k}$ [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]; in particular $\Gamma(U_k,\mathcal O_P)=S_{(x_k)}$ ([def-pc-proj]). (Directly: a point of $P$ is a homogeneous prime $\mathfrak p\not\supseteq S_+$; if $x_k\in\mathfrak p$ for all $k$ then $S_+=(x_0,\dots,x_m)\subseteq\mathfrak p$, so some $x_k\notin\mathfrak p$, i.e. $\mathfrak p\in U_k$.)

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01NG (lemma-standard-covering-projective-space), with Lemma 01MB (lemma-proj-scheme): 'D_+(f) is an affine scheme isomorphic to Spec(S_(f))'

proof.text: *Dehomogenization.* By [lem-weil-pbc-dehomogenization-polynomial-ring] with $n=m$, $T_i=x_i$ and $j=k$, the $A$-algebra map $\theta_k:A[Y_l:l\ne k]\to S_{(x_k)}$, $Y_l\mapsto x_l/x_k$, is an isomorphism (with inverse $a/x_k^e\mapsto a(Y_0,\dots,Y_{k-1},1,Y_{k+1},\dots,Y_m)$). With step 2 this gives $U_k\cong\operatorname{Spec}(S_{(x_k)})\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A[Y_l:l\ne k])=\mathbf A^m_A$, the isomorphism of Lemma 01NG.

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01NG, proof: 'Spec(Z[T_0/T_i,...,T_n/T_i]) = A^n_Z in an obvious way'

proof.text: *The intersections.* Let $k,l\in\{0,\dots,m\}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proj-basic-open-intersection] (with $f=x_k$, $g=x_l$), $U_k\cap U_l=D_+(x_kx_l)$ (directly: a homogeneous prime avoids $x_kx_l$ iff it avoids $x_k$ and $x_l$), a standard open, so $\Gamma(U_k\cap U_l,\mathcal O_P)=S_{(x_kx_l)}$ and the restriction maps $S_{(x_k)}\to S_{(x_kx_l)}$, $S_{(x_l)}\to S_{(x_kx_l)}$ are the graded localization maps $a/x_k^e\mapsto a x_l^e/(x_kx_l)^e$ ([def-pc-proj]). By [lem-weil-pbc-proj-basic-open-intersection] with $f=x_k$, $g=x_l$ and $d=e=1$, the preimage of $D_+(x_l)$ under the open immersion $\iota_{x_k}:\operatorname{Spec}S_{(x_k)}\to P$ with image $U_k$ is the principal open $D(x_l/x_k)$; equivalently $U_k\cap U_l$ is the basic open in the scheme $U_k$ of the function $x_l/x_k\in\Gamma(U_k,\mathcal O_P)=S_{(x_k)}$. In particular the restriction of $x_l/x_k$ to $U_k\cap U_l$ is a unit there, with inverse the restriction of $x_k/x_l\in S_{(x_l)}$ (in $S_{(x_kx_l)}$: $(x_lx_k/(x_kx_l))\cdot(x_kx_l/(x_kx_l))=1$).

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01M4 (lemma-standard-open) (1)(e) and Lemma 01MB (lemma-proj-scheme), proof: '$\varphi^{-1}(D(g))=D_+(h)$'; Lemma 01MC (lemma-proj-separated), proof: '$D_+(f)\cap D_+(g)=D_+(fg)$'

proof.text: *The twisting module on the charts.* By [def-pc-projective-space-twist] with $n=m$ and $d=1$, $\mathcal O_P(1)$ is glued from the free rank-one modules $\mathcal O_{U_i}e_i$, $e_i=e_i^{(1)}$, with transition rule $e_i=(x_i/x_j)e_j$ on $U_i\cap U_j$. So $\mathcal O_P(1)|_{U_k}$ is free with basis $e_k$, and taking $i=l$, $j=k$ gives $e_l=(x_l/x_k)e_k$ on $U_k\cap U_l$, where $x_l/x_k$ is the unit of step 4.

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01MS (lemma-when-invertible), proof: '$S\to S(nd)$, $x\mapsto f^nx$ becomes an isomorphism after inverting $f$' (with $f=x_k$, $d=n=1$: $\mathcal O_P(1)|_{U_k}$ is free on $x_k$)

proof.text: *The local structure morphisms.* For each $k$ let $q_k:U_k\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ be the composite of the isomorphism $U_k\cong\operatorname{Spec}(S_{(x_k)})$ of step 2 with $\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi_k)$, where $\varphi_k:A\to S_{(x_k)}$, $a\mapsto a/1$ (a ring map, as $A=S_0$) [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Under the bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] for $X=U_k$, $q_k$ corresponds to $\varphi_k:A\to S_{(x_k)}=\Gamma(U_k,\mathcal O_P)$.

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01ME (lemma-structure-morphism-proj), proof: 'This morphism, when restricted to $D_+(f)$ comes from the canonical ring map $S_0\to S_{(f)}$'

proof.text: *Agreement on overlaps.* Let $V=U_k\cap U_l$. For a morphism $h:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ and an open $V\subseteq X$, the global-sections ring map of $h|_V$ is that of $h$ followed by the restriction $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)\to\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_X)$ (functoriality of the comorphism). So $q_k|_V$ corresponds to $A\to S_{(x_k)}\to S_{(x_kx_l)}$, $a\mapsto a/1\mapsto a/1$, and $q_l|_V$ to $A\to S_{(x_l)}\to S_{(x_kx_l)}$, $a\mapsto a/1$, by step 4. The two ring maps $A\to\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_P)$ agree, so $q_k|_V=q_l|_V$ by the injectivity in [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] for $X=V$.

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01ME (lemma-structure-morphism-proj), proof: 'The maps $S\to S_f$, $S_{(f)}\to S_f$ are $S_0$-algebra maps'

proof.text: *Existence and uniqueness of $q$.* The $U_k$ cover $P$ (step 2) and the $q_k$ agree on all overlaps (step 7), so by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] there is a unique morphism $q:P\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ with $q|_{U_k}=q_k$ for all $k$, i.e. whose restriction to each $U_k=\operatorname{Spec}(S_{(x_k)})$ is induced by $a\mapsto a/1$; uniqueness of a morphism with these restrictions is the last clause of the same lemma. (This $q$ is Mathlib's \texttt{Proj.toSpecZero}, by \texttt{Proj.awayι\_toSpecZero}, with $S_0=A$.)
